targets.title: Effect of posture on levels of arousal and awareness in vegetative and minimally conscious patients: a preliminary investigation
targets.evidence_quote: In 2005 Elliott et al. published a paper entitled ‘Effect of posture on levels of arousal and awareness in vegetative and minimally conscious patients: a preliminary investigation’. Twelve patients, of whom 5 were in the vegetative state (VS) and 7 in the minimally conscious state (MCS), were assessed with the Wessex Head Injury Matrix (WHIM) when supine and when upright on a tilt table. The present study replicated and extended these findings by including a third position, sitting, in addition to supine and standing.
targets.outcome_quote: Most patients (75%) showed more behaviours when in the upright position, compared to lying down (p < .003). Our findings are similar to those seen in the study reported by Elliott et al.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Explicit author comparison says the findings are similar to the target; the additional sitting condition is an extension.
